title: Caching at Different Levels
unclear_source_points: The course's nearest-CDN wording is a useful latency model, but it does not distinguish geographical distance from routing, capacity, congestion, or resilience decisions.
The statement that almost all CDN population is lazy is qualitative; the source provides no measurement for the numerical emphasis.
The client-side viewing-progress example illustrates device-local staleness, but the source does not establish the named product's actual storage or synchronization design.
The remote cache is presented as centralized, but the source does not distinguish one logical shared service from its internal replication or sharding topology.
The advice that every remote-cache key needs an expiry is a safe course default, but the source does not separate expiry from capacity eviction or deliberately persistent entries.
The provider exercise does not specify a domain or origin prerequisite, cache headers, provider plan, proof headers, cost limit, cleanup, or how to protect account identifiers and secrets.
